- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underreacts to sentiment shifts; if sentiment flips from bullish to bearish within 3 days, adjust forecast downward by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent volatility; apply mean reversion: if 30d forecast is >+10% above 18d avg, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is flat, model often overpredicts; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 2–3 days to avoid false breakout.
